title: Document and gate the dangling provenance left by the 2026-09-10 repo recreation
description: Every @opum-ai/lore* version published before 0.6.1 carries SLSA provenance pinning a commit the 2026-09-10 repo delete/recreate destroyed. 0.6.0's attestation resolves to gitCommit 59ba30e497f8e98aa6c6be022d9363fd718fb4ee at refs/tags/v0.6.0; GitHub answers 422 'No commit found for SHA' for it, and its build run 34393976910 is 404. On npmjs.com this surfaces as a provenance link that cannot find the commit, which reads as tampering to anyone who does not know the history was rebuilt. The SHA still resolves in local clones' loose objects, so a git cat-file check wrongly says it is fine. Nothing repairs the existing links short of republishing. quest-cli confirmed the identical shape across all 8 of its pre-0.6.1 versions and already shipped the documented-not-repaired response in QCLI-267: a GitHub Release plus a --pre/--post provenance gate in release.yml. lore-cli has no equivalent. Filed 2026-09-13 out of the 0.6.1 release investigation; deliberately kept OUT of that release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release-publishing.md carries a section explaining that pre-0.6.1 provenance links are permanently dangling, names the 2026-09-10 recreation as the cause, and states plainly that this is expected rather than tampering
The doc warns that the destroyed SHAs still resolve in local clones loose objects, so git cat-file is not a valid check -- the live GitHub API is
release.yml carries a provenance gate comparable to quest-cli QCLI-267s --pre/--post check, so a future history rewrite is caught at release time rather than discovered on npmjs.com
A GitHub Release exists for the affected tags, or the decision not to create one is recorded with its reasoning
